chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Regarding the poor person who is given charity, does Zakat al-Fitr (Fitrana) fall upon him?' He said: 'Yes, he gives from what is given to him in charity.'

key_terms.زُرَارَةُ: Zurarah ibn A'yan, a prominent narrator
key_terms.صَدَقَةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (Fitrana), the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.يُتَصَدَّقُ عَلَيْهِ: He is given charity / He is the recipient of sadaqah

ai.seo_question: Does a poor person have to pay Zakat al-Fitr from their own pocket or from the charity they receive?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the poor are indeed obligated to pay Zakat al-Fitr, resolving a point of juristic discussion regarding their capacity. He specifies that their payment is drawn from the charity (sadaqah) they receive, effectively treating the received alms as their own wealth for this specific obligation, thereby ensuring the ritual's universality without imposing a double burden. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual and communal completeness of the fast, even for those with limited means.
